newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optiscan Imaging to list mid-August.
newsitem.headline: Optiscan Imaging to list mid-August.

text.p: Microscope manufacturer Optiscan Imaging Ltd said it expects to list on the Australian Stock Exchange around August 21.
The company is offering 15 million shares at 20 cents per share with a free attaching options to raise A$3 million.
Shares on issue will total 48.03 million, with existing shareholders retaining 69 percent of the company while the public holds 31 percent.
Major shareholders will include bioscience investor Circadian Technologies with 15.35 percent.
Optiscan produces confocal microscopes, which differ from ordinary light microscopes in the way in which a laser light is used to illuminate and observe a specimen.
Its major product is currently a desktop confocal microscope, the Optiscan F900e, with a list price of A$90,000.

However, in its prospectus, the company said it was focussing its efforts on developing its confocal endomicroscope which utilises optical fibres, allowing it to be small enough to be inserted into the human body.

The laser and and optical fibre based product would allow non-invasive disease monitoring and diagnosis as it would mean living tissue could be examined in situ at the cellular level, the company said.
Market release of the new product is planned for 1999.
